related_questions.question: Can toenails indicate a health problem?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, toenails can indicate various health problems. Changes in color, texture, and shape can be signs of underlying conditions, ranging from minor issues like fungal infections to more serious concerns like skin cancer, diabetes, or kidney disease.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, toenails can indicate various health problems

list.title: Yellow or Brownish Nails:
list.snippet: Often associated with fungal infections, but can also be a sign of psoriasis or excessive use of nail polish.

list.title: Black or Purple Nails:
list.snippet: Can indicate a bruise (subungual hematoma) from injury, but also potentially vitamin B12 deficiency, anemia, or even melanoma.

list.title: Blue Nails:
list.snippet: May be related to Raynaud's phenomenon, where poor circulation leads to bluish discoloration, or potentially heart problems.

list.title: White Spots or Streaks:
list.snippet: Can indicate injury, infection, or nutritional deficiencies, including iron or zinc deficiencies.

list.title: Dark Streaks or Bands:
list.snippet: While more common in people with darker skin tones, dark streaks can be a sign of melanoma (skin cancer) in rare cases.
Thickened Nails: Can be caused by fungal infections, aging, or circulation problems.
Spoon-Shaped Nails (Koilonychia): Often associated with iron-deficiency anemia.
Clubbing: Characterized by nails curving around the fingertips, which may indicate lung, heart, or liver issues.
Pitting: Small depressions in the nail surface, linked to psoriasis or alopecia (hair loss).
Cracking or Splitting: Can be caused by fungal infections, thyroid issues, or harsh chemicals.
Slow-Growing Nails: May indicate poor circulation, malnutrition, or hypothyroidism.
Nail Separation from the Nail Bed (Onycholysis): Can result from injury, fungal infections, or exposure to chemicals.
Beau's Lines: Grooves across the nail, possibly linked to high fever, stress, or vascular disease.
Any new or changing dark streaks or bands on the nail.
Any unexplained discoloration or thickening of the nail.
Nail separation from the nail bed.
Changes in nail shape or texture that are concerning.
Any pain, swelling, or discharge around the nail.

text_blocks.snippet: Paying attention to your toenails can be an early indicator of various health problems. If you notice any changes, it's best to consult with a podiatrist or other healthcare professional for proper diagnosis and treatment, says Ashley Dikis, an assistant professor at Des Moines University College of Podiatric Medicine and Surgery.

related_questions.question: What do nails look like with heart problems?

text_blocks.snippet: Nails can exhibit several changes that may indicate heart problems. These include blue or pale coloration, clubbing (widening and rounding of the fingertips), splinter hemorrhages (thin red or reddish-brown lines under the nails), and koilonychia (spoon-shaped nails). While some nail changes can be harmless, it's important to consult a doctor if you notice any persistent or concerning changes in your nails, especially if accompanied by other symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, or fatigue.
snippet_highlighted_words: blue or pale coloration, clubbing (widening and rounding of the fingertips), splinter hemorrhages (thin red or reddish-brown lines under the nails), and koilonychia (spoon-shaped nails)

text_blocks.snippet: Specific nail changes associated with heart problems:

list.title: Clubbing:
list.snippet: This involves the fingertips becoming enlarged and the nails curving downwards, resembling a club or spoon. It can be a sign of low oxygen levels in the blood, which can be linked to heart conditions like congenital heart defects or heart failure.

list.title: Splinter Hemorrhages:
list.snippet: These are thin, reddish-brown lines that appear under the nails, and they can indicate inflammation of the heart's inner lining (endocarditis).

list.title: Pale Nails:
list.snippet: Very pale nails can be a sign of anemia, congestive heart failure, or liver disease.

list.title: Blue or Pale Nails:
list.snippet: A bluish or pale tint in the nails can indicate low oxygen levels in the blood, which may be related to heart or lung problems.

list.title: Koilonychia (Spoon Nails):
list.snippet: In this condition, the nails become abnormally thin and concave, with a spoon-like shape. It can be associated with anemia, hemochromatosis, and heart disease.

list.title: Terry's Nails:
list.snippet: Most of the nail appears white with a narrow band of pink at the tip. While this can be a normal part of aging, it can also be a sign of liver, kidney, or heart problems.

list.title: Pitted Nails:
list.snippet: Circulatory problems related to heart disease or uncontrolled diabetes can cause ridges, grooves, or pitting on the toenails.
